visual.general_description: Eleven-month clinical timeline of one patient combining symptom-intensity mounds, menstruation, hospitalization and per-drug dose bars.
visual.detailed_description: White background, 693 x 376 px. A row of month labels X, X+1 ... X+10 runs across the top, separated by dotted vertical lines. A rounded legend box at upper right shows a green swatch "Hallucinatory delusional state" and a yellow swatch "Manic state". The first row, labelled "Intensity of sychiatric symptoms" (printed without the initial p), has three green mounds: a large wide one at the X+1 column and two narrower ones at X+2 and X+3, followed by seven yellow mounds from the X+4 column onward: a narrow one at X+4, a wide one at X+5, narrow and wider ones around the X+5/X+6 and X+6/X+7 boundaries, a narrow one near the X+7/X+8 boundary, a smaller one at X+8 and a tiny one at X+9. The "Menstruation" row shows nine red vertical bars on an arrow line: one in the X+1 column, none in the X+2 and X+3 columns, one in each of the X+4 to X+9 columns, a solid red bar at the X+9/X+10 boundary over which the dotted month separator is drawn (the separators are drawn on top of other elements, e.g. also visible through mounds), and one in the X+10 column. A row labelled "Drospirenone (3 mg/day)" and "Ethinyl estradiol (0.02 mg/day)" has a pink bar starting within the X+7 column and running to the right edge. Below, blue stepped bars per drug: RIS from the X+1 column to about the X+3/X+4 boundary (Min 1, Max 8 mg/day); OLZ from X+1 with stepped changes (Min 5, Max 20 mg/day), stepping down near the end of X+9 and ending with a lowest step just past the X+9/X+10 separator, inside the X+10 column; APZ in two separate bars, the first from within the X+3 column to within the X+5 column (Min 12, Max 30 mg/day) and the second from about X+9 to the right edge (Min 6, Max 24 mg/day); BREX short stepped bar spanning the X+5 and X+6 columns (Min 1, Max 2 mg/day); a dotted grey arrow separates the antipsychotics from the mood stabilizers; VPA first bar from the X+4 column to about the X+5/X+6 boundary labelled 400 mg/day and a second bar from about the X+6/X+7 boundary to the right edge with a raised block (Max 1000 mg/day) and a lowered segment (Min 200 mg/day); Li short bar between them within X+6 (Min 200, Max 600 mg/day), with a short raised step at its right end before it stops. A cyan "Hospitalization" band begins near the left of the X+1 column and extends to the right edge of the timeline.

limitations: Timeline of one patient: month-column labels are the only time scale; no day-level scale, y-axis numbers or intensity values are printed.
Peak, bar and band positions relative to month columns are approximate at the available 693 x 376 resolution; start and end of bars are not read as exact dates.
Printed Min/Max dose labels are recorded as shown; the figure does not print a dose for each month or step.

evidence.quote: We describe a 19-year-old Japanese woman with no psychiatric history who presented with acute mania and psychosis necessitating hospitalization.

pixel_observations: Month labels X through X+10 with dotted vertical separators; no calendar dates or day scale.
Legend: green = "Hallucinatory delusional state"; yellow = "Manic state"; y-axis label printed as "Intensity of sychiatric symptoms".
Three green mounds (largest at X+1, narrower at X+2 and X+3) and seven yellow mounds (X+4 to X+9, tallest/widest near X+5, small at X+8, tiny at X+9).

Nine red menstruation bars: one in the X+1 column, none in the X+2 and X+3 columns, one in each of X+4 to X+9, a solid red bar at the X+9/X+10 boundary with the dotted month separator drawn over it and one in X+10. The figure does not label any interval as amenorrhea.
Pink drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol bar begins inside the X+7 column and continues to the right edge.
Printed dose labels: RIS Min 1 / Max 8; OLZ Min 5 / Max 20; APZ Min 12 / Max 30 and Min 6 / Max 24; BREX Min 1 / Max 2; VPA 400, Max 1000, Min 200; Li Min 200 / Max 600 (all mg/day).
Cyan hospitalization band runs from near the start of the X+1 column across the remainder of the timeline to the right edge.
No faces, body parts, text identifiers, dates or device text are present.

Magnified view: the OLZ bar steps down late in the X+9 column and its lowest final step extends just past the X+9/X+10 dotted separator into the X+10 column; the second APZ bar begins inside the X+9 column.
Magnified view: the Li bar is a low block through most of X+6 with a short raised step (the Max 600 mg/day level) at its right end; the figure does not mark when tremor occurred.

assignments.subject: patient

evidence.quote: The clinical course—encompassing psychiatric symptoms, menstrual cycles, and interventions—is summarized in Figure 1.

Eleven-month clinical timeline. Psychiatric symptom intensity (green peaks = psychosis; yellow peaks = mania), menstruation (red bars), hospitalization (light blue band), and antipsychotic/mood-stabilizer periods with dose ranges (blue bars; RIS = risperidone, OLZ, olanzapine; APZ, aripiprazole; BREX, brexpiprazole; VPA, valproate; Li, lithium). A pink marker denotes initiation of drospirenone 3 mg/ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg in Month X + 7.

assignments.rationale: The index-patient case description calls out Figure 1 as the clinical course (psychiatric symptoms, menstrual cycles, interventions) and the caption describes the same months and drug timeline; ownership rests on the text, not on appearance.
